court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Mukesh Kumar vs Union Of India General Manager
facts_of_case: Jagdish Harijan was an employee of Indian Railways. He had two wives, Gayatri Devi and Konika Devi. Appellant No.1 Mukesh Kumar is his son through his second wife. Jagdish Harijan died in service on 24.02.2014.

legal_principles.principle: A condition imposed by an employer must have a reasonable nexus to the object sought to be achieved.
legal_principles.held: The salutary purpose underlying the grant of compassionate appointment, which is to prevent destitution and penury in the family of a deceased employee requires that any stipulation or condition which is imposed must have or bear a reasonable nexus to the object which is sought to be achieved.

legal_principles.principle: A policy or rule cannot be inconsistent with Article 14 of the Constitution.
legal_principles.held: However, it is not open to the State, while making the scheme or rules, to lay down a condition which is inconsistent with Article 14 of the Constitution.
cited_cases: Mukesh Kumar vs Union Of India General Manager, (2022)
use_in: cases involving equal treatment and non-discrimination

legal_principles.principle: A condition that excludes a class of beneficiaries who have been deemed legitimate by the operation of law is disproportionate to the object sought to be achieved.
legal_principles.held: By excluding a class of beneficiaries who have been deemed legitimate by the operation of law, the condition imposed is disproportionate to the object sought to be achieved.
cited_cases: Mukesh Kumar vs Union Of India General Manager, (2022)

outcome.final_order: The condition imposed by the Railway Board circular that compassionate appointment cannot be granted to children born from the second wife of a deceased employee is legally unsustainable.
